
```{r}
# Unlike every tab above, this one is about the organisation as a whole rather
# than about one package: one tab per channel the community is reached through.
views_by_video <- latest_youtube_views_by_video()

# The feed carries every post ever made, with the date it was written and the
# likes and reposts it has gathered since (those are the numbers each post has
# now, not what it had then).
bsky_all_posts <- bsky_posts()

no_feed <- paste(
  "No posts collected yet: the Bluesky feed could not be read the last time",
  "the data was refreshed."
)

# Posts run long and hold newlines, so both the table and the chart show the
# opening of a post rather than the whole of it.
bsky_excerpt <- function(text, n = 140) {
  flat <- trimws(gsub("\\s+", " ", text))
  paste0(
    htmltools::htmlEscape(substr(flat, 1, n)),
    ifelse(nchar(flat) > n, "…", "")
  )
}

# What a post gathers on average. Like the counters above, these are the numbers
# the posts hold now rather than what they held when they were written.
# `replies` is read from the feed only as of this version of fetch.R, so it is
# missing from posts collected before the next refresh.
bsky_average <- function(metric) {
  values <- bsky_all_posts[[metric]]
  if (is.null(values)) {
    return(NA)
  }
  round(mean(values), 1)
}
```

###### Row

```{r}
# Youtube only reports the views a video has now, so this is a snapshot rather
# than a series: one point per talk, placed on the day it was published and at
# the number of views it has reached since. Older talks have had longer to
# gather views, so the trend along the x axis is expected rather than telling.
views_by_video |>
  arrange(published) |> 
  e_charts(x = published) |>
  e_line(serie = views, bind = title) |>
  e_scatter(serie = views, bind = title, symbol_size = 12) |>
  e_legend(show = FALSE) |>
  e_tooltip(
    # `bind` above puts the talk in `params.name`; the point itself is
    # [publication date, views].
    formatter = htmlwidgets::JS(
      # `parseFloat` because echarts4r pads the values to a common width
      "function(params) {
         return params.name + '<br/><strong>' + parseFloat(params.value[1]) +
           '</strong> views since ' + params.value[0];
       }"
    ),
    extraCssText = "max-width: 25rem; white-space: normal;"
  ) |>
  e_datazoom(type = "slider") |> 
  e_toolbox(show = FALSE) |>
  e_title("Views per talk", subtext = "By date of publication")
```

```{r}
#| title: Views per talk
views_by_video |>
  mutate(
    title = paste0(
      "<a href=\"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=",
      video_id,
      "\" target=\"_blank\">",
      htmltools::htmlEscape(title),
      "</a>"
    )
  ) |>
  select(published, title, views) |>
  reactable(
    columns = list(
      published = colDef(name = "Published"),
      title = colDef(name = "Talk", html = TRUE),
      views = colDef(name = "Views")
    ),
    defaultSorted = list(views = "desc"),
    searchable = TRUE,
    highlight = TRUE
  )
```

```{r}
bsky_all_posts |>
    count(date, name = "n_posts") |>
    arrange(date) |>
    mutate(posts = cumsum(n_posts)) |>
    e_charts(x = date) |>
    e_line(serie = posts, name = "Posts") |>
    e_legend(show = FALSE) |>
    e_tooltip(trigger = "axis") |>
    e_datazoom(type = "slider") |> 
    e_toolbox(show = FALSE) |>
    e_title(
      "Posts over time",
      subtext = "Cumulative, excluding replies and reposts"
    )
```

#### Website

```{r}
# Visits to palaeoverse.org and its subdomains over the past month, as reported
# by GoatCounter. "Visitors" rather than pageviews: GoatCounter counts a person
# once per page per day.
site_pages <- website_pages()
site_countries <- .website_stats()$countries
# First day of the window covered, as "5 July 2026"
website_since <- function() {
  since <- .website_stats()$since
  if (is.null(since)) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  format(since, "%e %B %Y") |> trimws()
}
site_period <- paste("Past 30 days, since", website_since())

missing_token <- paste(
  "No data collected yet. The GoatCounter API needs a token with the",
  "\"read statistics\" permission, passed to fetch.R as GOATCOUNTER_TOKEN."
)
```

####### Row

```{r}
#| title: Most visited pages
table <- site_pages |>
    mutate(
      # The scheme is the same on every row and only takes up width
      url = paste0(
        "<a href=\"",
        url,
        "\" target=\"_blank\">",
        htmltools::htmlEscape(sub("^https://", "", url)),
        "</a>"
      )
    ) |>
    select(url, title, visitors) |>
    reactable(
      columns = list(
        url = colDef(name = "Page", html = TRUE),
        title = colDef(name = "Title"),
        visitors = colDef(name = "Visitors")
      ),
      defaultSorted = list(visitors = "desc"),
      searchable = TRUE,
      highlight = TRUE
    )
  # The chart on the right says which period it covers in its subtitle; this
  # card has a table rather than a chart, so the same note goes above it.
  htmltools::tagList(
    htmltools::tags$p(site_period, class = "card-note"),
    table
  )

```

```{r}
#| title: Visitors by country
  countries_map <- website_countries_map()
  scale <- interpolate_palette(
    data = countries_map,
    column = "visitors",
    method = "quantile",
    n = 4,
    palette = colorRampPalette(c("#E0F2FA", "#64BDD8", "#0D725A"))
  )

  maplibre(
    style = carto_style("positron"),
    projection = "mercator"
  ) |>
    add_fill_layer(
      id = "countries",
      source = countries_map,
      fill_color = scale$expression,
      fill_opacity = 0.75,
      fill_outline_color = "#FFFFFF",
      tooltip = "tooltip",
      hover_options = list(fill_opacity = 1)
    ) |>
    add_legend(
      paste("Visitors since", website_since()),
      values = get_legend_labels(scale, digits = 0),
      colors = get_legend_colors(scale),
      type = "continuous",
      position = "bottom-right"
    )
```
